selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the first benefit of giving a person’s life and belongings to Allah?
questions.answer: What does not last in this world becomes lasting in the next life.

questions.question: What picture does the passage use to show that moments of life are not wasted?
questions.answer: It compares them to seeds that later show beautiful results.

questions.question: Which ability is first shown as either helpful or harmful?
questions.answer: The intelligence.

questions.question: Why does the passage say some sinful people run to drinking or pointless fun?
questions.answer: They want to escape the pain caused by their troubled minds.

questions.question: What is one right use of the eye?
questions.answer: Seeing Allah’s artistry and signs in the world.

questions.question: What body part is connected with the sense of taste?
questions.answer: The tongue.

questions.question: What are readers told to compare with the mind, eye, and tongue?
questions.answer: All the other body parts and abilities.

questions.question: What should a person do because of this weakness and need?
questions.answer: Depend on Allah and trust Him.

questions.question: How can a person face these facts in the right way?
questions.answer: By depending on Allah and trusting Him.

questions.question: What is the fifth benefit?
questions.answer: The acts of worship done with one’s body and senses will return as fruits of Paradise at the time of greatest need.

questions.question: What change happens to short worldly life when it is given for Allah?
questions.answer: It turns into something everlasting.

questions.question: What is the second profit stated in the passage?
questions.answer: Paradise is given as the price.

questions.question: What happens when intelligence is controlled by the nafs instead of being used for Allah?
questions.answer: It becomes harmful and fills a person with heavy worries.

questions.question: What does this teach about intelligence by itself?
questions.answer: It can help or hurt depending on how it is used.

questions.question: What is the eye able to become if it is used for Allah?
questions.answer: A noble observer of Allah’s signs and artistry.

questions.question: Why does the passage speak directly to the intelligence, eye, and tongue?
questions.answer: To help the reader clearly notice the difference between low use and noble use.

questions.question: What should a reader do with the other limbs and senses after hearing these examples?
questions.answer: Compare them in the same way.

questions.question: What should a person do because of these weaknesses?
questions.answer: Put trust in Allah and submit to Him.

questions.question: What happens to the conscience without this reliance?
questions.answer: It stays disturbed and full of pain.

questions.question: When will that reward be given?
questions.answer: At the moment when a person needs it most.

questions.question: What is the first profit trying to teach about life in this world?
questions.answer: If life is used for Allah, it does not end in loss but continues with lasting reward.

questions.question: What is the second benefit named in the passage?
questions.answer: A person receives Paradise as the great payment.

questions.question: What is one wrong way to use intelligence?
questions.answer: Using it for selfish desires instead of for Allah.

questions.question: What does rightly used intelligence open up for a person?
questions.answer: Understanding of Allah’s mercy and wisdom in creation.
